doc:010.title: First Postoperative Progress Note from Breast Surgery
doc:010.content: Local anesthesia. Core needle biopsy of right breast mass. The patient was placed in the supine position, and routine disinfection and draping were performed. A puncture site in the right nipple-areolar region was selected, and local infiltration anesthesia was administered subcutaneously and around the mass using 1% lidocaine. A 3mm small incision was made at the puncture site. Under ultrasound guidance, multiple biopsy samples were obtained using a spring-loaded core needle and submitted for rapid paraffin pathology. The puncture site was disinfected again and dressed with a pressure bandage. The procedure was completed. Postoperatively, the incision was dressed with a chest compression bandage. Closely monitor vital signs and observe the wound for active bleeding or oozing.

doc:014.title: First Postoperative Progress Note from Breast Surgery
doc:014.content: General anesthesia. Right breast-conserving surgery for breast cancer + sentinel lymph node biopsy + fascial tissue flap reconstruction [breast conservation + sentinel lymph node]. The patient was placed supine with both upper extremities abducted. After induction of anesthesia, the surgical field was disinfected and draped. 5ml methylene blue was injected into the right areolar region, followed by massage for 5 minutes. A No. 10 blade was used to make a curved right axillary incision approximately 5cm in length. The skin and subcutaneous fat were divided layer by layer with electrocautery to enter the axilla. The first-echelon blue-stained lymph node was identified by following the blue-stained axillary lymphatic vessels, excised, and submitted for intraoperative frozen-section examination. The results showed: “Right axillary para-sentinel lymph node 1”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary para-sentinel lymph node 2”: macrometastatic carcinoma was identified in 1/1 lymph nodes on frozen section. “Right axillary para-sentinel lymph node 3”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary para-sentinel lymph node 4”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary sentinel lymph node 1”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary sentinel lymph node 2”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary sentinel lymph node 3”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. “Right axillary sentinel lymph node 4”: no metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph node on frozen section. Right breast-conserving surgery for breast cancer was then performed. An incision approximately 5 cm long was made through the skin and subcutaneous tissue. The edge of the skin flap was elevated, and electrocautery was used to perform undermining dissection between the subcutaneous fat and glandular tissue. The mass and more than 2cm of the surrounding breast tissue were widely excised down to the pectoralis major fascia, with partial excision of the pectoralis major fascia. Sutures and titanium clips were used to mark each margin of the specimen. Intraoperative mammography confirmed complete excision of the mass. The margins were submitted for frozen-section pathological examination, which showed that the suture-marked “superior, medial, inferior, and lateral margins” of the “right breast-conserving specimen” were all free of carcinoma. The margins were negative. Meticulous hemostasis was achieved. After placement of titanium clips, fascial tissue around the residual cavity was mobilized and transferred as a tissue flap for reconstruction. 2-0 silk sutures were used for ligation and fixation. The residual cavity and subcutaneous layer were closed with interrupted 4-0 silk sutures, and the skin was closed with a continuous intradermal suture using 4-0 slowly absorbable Vicryl. The procedure was completed. Postoperatively, the wound was dressed with a compressive chest band, and routine fluid replacement and supportive treatment were provided. Vital signs were closely monitored, with attention to any active bleeding or oozing from the wound.

doc:030.title: First ward-round note by the attending physician of breast surgery
doc:030.content: The patient has no history of taking hormone-containing foods or medications and has a family history of breast cancer. 1. The patient is an elderly woman. 2. The patient was admitted because a right breast mass had been found on physical examination for 10 days, with intermittent stabbing pain in the right breast for 2 months. 3. Physical examination revealed symmetric breasts; the skin of both breasts showed no redness, swelling, ulceration, dimpling, or peau d'orange changes; the bilateral nipples were at the same level, without retraction or deviation, and there were no eczematous changes of the nipples. A mass approximately 2 cm in diameter was palpable in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast; it was hard, poorly mobile, and poorly defined, without adhesion to the skin or obvious tenderness. There was no discharge. No definite mass was palpable in the contralateral breast. No abnormally enlarged lymph nodes were palpable in either axilla or either supraclavicular region. 4. Ancillary examinations: 2124-07-26 Breast ultrasonography at outside Hospital A: a 20*22mm hypoechoic lesion was seen in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast, with a poorly defined boundary, spiculated margins, and an irregular shape, BI-RADS category 5. An enlarged lymph node measuring approximately 11*6mm was seen in the right axilla. 2124-07-26 Mammography at outside Hospital A: an irregular mass in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast, BI-RADS category 5. 1. Mammary lobular hyperplasia: mammary lobular hyperplasia is common in premenopausal women, with breast pain related to the menstrual cycle and a nodular sensation of breast thickening on physical examination as its main clinical manifestations. The breast pain has no fixed location, may persist throughout the menstrual cycle, and is relieved after the onset of menstruation; on examination, a nodular sensation or localized thickening may be palpable in the upper outer quadrant of the breast. This patient is a 72-year-old woman; the mass is poorly defined, without skin adhesion, and no enlarged lymph nodes are palpable in the ipsilateral axilla; therefore, this is not consistent with this diagnosis. 2. Paget disease of the nipple: patients with Paget disease of the nipple mostly present with eczematous changes of the nipple-areolar skin, local skin redness, mild erosion and serous exudation, and thickened and hardened skin with clear boundaries. Pruritus or burning pain is often present. This patient has no symptoms such as pruritus or erosion of the nipple and areola; therefore, this disease is not currently considered likely. 1. The patient has completed a complete blood count, liver and renal function tests, electrolyte and blood glucose tests, routine urinalysis, and coagulation function tests. No contraindications to surgery were identified. The specific treatment plan will be determined after the patient completes preoperative imaging examinations. 2. The patient has a previous history of atrial fibrillation and is currently receiving anticoagulation. Echocardiography has been completed, and consultations with the departments of cardiology and anesthesiology have been requested.

doc:031.content: *** Chief Physician Ward Round: The patient underwent core needle biopsy of the right breast mass under local anesthesia yesterday and reported no particular discomfort today. Physical examination: The patient's demeanor and mental status were acceptable; vital signs were stable. Morning temperature was 36.5 °C, and heart rate was 74 beats/min. A chest bandage was in place for compression. The puncture site was healing well, dry, and without exudate; no subcutaneous ecchymosis was observed. Ancillary examination: 2124-08-01 Color Doppler ultrasonography of the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, kidneys, and portal vein: fatty liver; intrahepatic cystic lesion, considered a hepatic cyst, follow-up recommended; no obvious abnormalities were observed in the gallbladder, pancreatic body, spleen, or kidneys; no obvious abnormality was observed in portal venous blood flow. Management: 1. The dressing was changed once, and wound healing will continue to be observed. 2. Await the pathology results of the core needle biopsy specimen to determine the subsequent surgical approach.

doc:035.title: Breast surgery preoperative discussion record
doc:035.content: ***, Chief Physician; ***, Attending Physician; ***, Resident Physician. The patient discovered a right breast mass during a physical examination 10 days ago, without tenderness or localized skin ulceration, redness, or swelling of the breast; whether there was skin thinning; no dilated subcutaneous veins were seen, and there were no eczematous changes of the nipple skin. No nipple discharge. On 2124-07-26, the patient underwent breast ultrasonography at Outside Hospital A, which showed a 20*22mm hypoechoic lesion in the upper outer right breast, with a poorly defined boundary, spiculated margins, and irregular morphology, BI-RADS category 5. An enlarged lymph node measuring approximately 11*6mm was seen in the right axilla. Mammography showed an irregular mass in the upper outer right breast, BI-RADS category 5. For further diagnosis and treatment, the patient was admitted from the outpatient clinic with a provisional diagnosis of “right breast mass, suspected carcinoma.” Since onset, the patient has been alert, with fair mental status, sleep, and appetite; bowel movements and urination have been normal, and there has been no significant weight gain or loss. Physical examination: Both breasts were symmetrical; the skin of both breasts showed no redness, swelling, ulceration, depression, or peau d’orange changes; both nipples were at the same level, without retraction or deviation, and there were no eczematous changes of the nipples. A mass approximately 2 cm in diameter was palpable in the upper outer right breast; it was hard, poorly mobile, and poorly demarcated, without adhesion to the skin or significant tenderness. No discharge. No definite mass was palpable in the contralateral breast. No abnormally enlarged lymph nodes were palpable in either axilla or either supraclavicular region. 1. Needle biopsy pathology of the patient's right breast mass indicated malignancy, constituting an indication for surgical resection. 2. The patient was fully informed of the necessity and risks of surgery, expressed understanding, and consented to surgery. 3. The patient has completed the relevant examinations, with no obvious contraindications to surgery identified. Right breast-conserving surgery for breast cancer + sentinel lymph node biopsy, with possible axillary lymph node dissection and possible simple mastectomy for right breast cancer. Whether staged surgery is required: No. General condition was fair, vital signs were stable, cardiopulmonary examination was unremarkable, body temperature was normal, contraindications to surgery had been excluded, and the indications were clear. 1. Bleeding: meticulous hemostasis during surgery. 2. Infection: strict aseptic technique. 3. Injury to surrounding nerves and soft tissues: careful manipulation. *** Resident Physician's opinion: Needle biopsy pathology of the patient's right breast mass indicated malignancy, requiring surgical treatment. *** Attending Physician's opinion: In conjunction with the patient's imaging findings, right breast cancer has been confirmed; therefore, right breast-conserving surgery will be performed. If an intraoperative margin is positive, the margin will be re-excised; if it remains positive, simple mastectomy for right breast cancer will be performed. *** Chief Physician's opinion: Agree to perform right breast-conserving surgery for breast cancer + sentinel lymph node biopsy, with possible axillary lymph node dissection and possible simple mastectomy for right breast cancer. Agree to perform right breast-conserving surgery for breast cancer + sentinel lymph node biopsy, with possible axillary lymph node dissection and possible simple mastectomy for right breast cancer.

ehr:terminal:001.title: Final Inpatient Status and Discharge Disposition
ehr:terminal:001.content: During this hospitalization, surgery for the primary right breast lesion and the axillary surgery documented in the source record were completed; the discharge diagnosis was malignant neoplasm of the upper outer quadrant of the breast, the treatment outcome was cured, and the discharge disposition was discharge on medical advice.

img:001.title: Inpatient MRI
img:001.content:
Mass in the upper outer right breast; local postoperative changes in both breasts; cortical thickening of the right axillary lymph nodes, with visualization of the right internal mammary lymph nodes. Please correlate with contrast-enhanced breast MRI.
Plain scan: Local postoperative changes in both breasts. The skin surfaces of both breasts are mildly irregular. No obvious thickening of the skin or areolae is seen, neither nipple is retracted, and the subcutaneous structures have clear layers. The glandular tissue of both breasts is scattered in distribution and approximately symmetric. A mass is visible in the upper outer right breast, showing isointense signal on T1W, slightly hyperintense signal on T2W, and hyperintense signal on DWI, with an ADC value of approximately 0.9×10-3mm2/s. No abnormal signal is seen in the retromammary spaces bilaterally. The cortex of the right axillary lymph nodes is thickened. No obviously enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the left axilla. The right internal mammary lymph nodes are visualized.
